title: RTPS Removed the limit to the datatype number of elements
description:
The DataType must be parsed completely due to nested types. Putting a
limit on it might create issues when dissecting the user data samples.

Can someone review this task, please?
there is no risk of big loop ?

It has to be a really big number for that. Much bigger than what makes sense with RTPS DataType (DataType is the definition of the user data kind. But not the data itself).

RTPS protocol options allow limiting the number of members in RTPS user data structs and arrays. There is where the workload can be really heavy in big types. However, processing the full DataType (that is done here) is required to know the member offsets later.
Yes but a malformed pcap can be set a big value ?
Could be but the chances are minimum. At some point, the offset would be bigger than the holder tree size.

Hi @ismaelrti,  could you please take a look at these warnings from recent buildbot runs:

 ** (tshark:13146) 16:51:29.516369 [Epan WARNING] epan/proto.c:8473 -- tmp_fld_check_assert(): Field 'entityKind' (rtps.sm.entityId.entityKind) has a conflicting entry in its value_string: 135 is at indices 13 (RTI Built-in reader (with key)) and 15 (Object normal meta CST reader)
 
** (tshark:13146) 16:51:29.517817 [Epan WARNING] epan/proto.c:8473 -- tmp_fld_check_assert(): Field 'readerEntityKind' (rtps.sm.rdEntityId.entityKind) has a conflicting entry in its value_string: 135 is at indices 13 (RTI Built-in reader (with key)) and 15 (Object normal meta CST reader)

** (tshark:13146) 16:51:29.519187 [Epan WARNING] epan/proto.c:8473 -- tmp_fld_check_assert(): Field 'writerEntityKind' (rtps.sm.wrEntityId.entityKind) has a conflicting entry in its value_string: 135 is at indices 13 (RTI Built-in reader (with key)) and 15 (Object normal meta CST reader)

** (tshark:13146) 16:51:29.520585 [Epan WARNING] epan/proto.c:8473 -- tmp_fld_check_assert(): Field 'entityKind' (rtps.param.guid.entityKind) has a conflicting entry in its value_string: 135 is at indices 13 (RTI Built-in reader (with key)) and 15 (Object normal meta CST reader)

It seems that:
ENTITYKIND_RTI_BUILTIN_READER_WITH_KEY and
ENTITYID_OBJECT_NORMAL_META_CST_READER
both have the value 0x87, so in entity_kind_vals[], the first one hides the second.

I tried to work it out from https://community.rti.com/static/documentation/connext-micro/2.4.11/doc/html/rtps__rtps_8h_source.html, but wasn't sure how to map between the enums there and the #defines in the dissector..
Thanks Martin. I have created a different merge request for this https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9739
Yes, that's fine - flagging it here was the lazy/easy way to tell you
